title.zh: 卷二百七十一 列傳第三十 馬令琮 杜漢徽 張廷翰 吳虔裕 蔡審廷 周廣 張勳 石曦 張藏英 陸萬友 解暉 李韜 王晉卿 郭廷謂 趙延進 輔超
title.en: Volume 271 Biographies 30: Ma Lingcong, Du Hanhui, Zhang Tinghan, Wu Qianyu, Cai Shenting, Zhou Guang, Zhang Xun, Shi Xi, Zhang Cang Ying, Lu Wanyou, Jie Hui, Li Tao, Wang Jinqing, Guo Tingwei, Zhao Yanjin, Fu Chao
title.raw: 卷二百七十一 列傳第三十 馬令琮 杜漢徽 張廷翰 吳虔裕 蔡審廷 周廣 張勳 石曦 張藏英 陸萬友 解暉 李韜 王晉卿 郭廷謂 趙延進 輔超 Volume 271 Biographies 30: Ma Lingcong, Du Hanhui, Zhang Tinghan, Wu Qianyu, Cai Shenting, Zhou Guang, Zhang Xun, Shi Xi, Zhang Cang Ying, Lu Wanyou, Jie Hui, Li Tao, Wang Jinqing, Guo Tingwei, Zhao Yanjin, Fu Chao

sentences.zh: 馬令琮

translations.literal: Ma Lingcong
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lingcong

sentences.zh: 馬令琮，本名令威，避周祖名改之，大名人。

translations.literal: Ma Lingcong, original name Lingwei, changed to avoid the Zhou Founder's taboo name, a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lingcong, whose original name was Lingwei, changed it to avoid the taboo on the Zhou founder's name; he was a native of Daming.

sentences.zh: 父全節，《五代史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Quanjie has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quanjie is the subject of a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 全節歷橫海、定遠、昭義、彰德、定武、天雄六節度，皆署令琮為牙校，累授彰德牙內都指揮使、檢校尚書左僕射，領勤州刺史。

translations.literal: Quanjie successively held six military governorships—Henghai, Dingyuan, Zhaoyi, Zhangde, Dingwu, and Tianxiong—and in each appointed Lingcong as a yamen staff officer; he was repeatedly promoted to Zhangde's inner yamen commander-in-chief, acting Minister of the Left in the Department of State Affairs, and concurrently Prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanjie served in turn as military governor of Henghai, Dingyuan, Zhaoyi, Zhangde, Dingwu, and Tianxiong, and in each post appointed Lingcong to his personal staff. Lingcong rose to become inner yamen commander-in-chief at Zhangde, acting Minister of the Left, and concurrently prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 令琮少善騎射，嘗從其父平安州及與鎮州安重榮戰，皆有功，由是知名。

translations.literal: Lingcong from youth excelled at mounted archery; he once followed his father to pacify Pingzhou and fought An Chongrong of Zhenzhou, distinguishing himself in both, and thereby became well known.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Lingcong was skilled in horsemanship and archery. He accompanied his father in the pacification of Pingzhou and in the campaign against An Chongrong of Zhenzhou, earning merit in both, and thus won a reputation.

sentences.zh: 晉開運二年，全節卒，令琮起復，拜隰州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun of Jin, Quanjie died; Lingcong resumed office from mourning and was appointed Prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Kaiyun era of Later Jin (945), Quanjie died. Lingcong left mourning to take office and was appointed prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 漢祖開國，為西京巡檢使。

translations.literal: When the Han founder established the state, he became Western Capital inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Han established his dynasty, Lingcong was made inspection commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 周祖受命，改陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder received the Mandate, he was changed to Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou founder took the throne, Lingcong was transferred to be prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 征兗州，為京城四門外巡檢。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Yanzhou, he served as inspector outside the four gates of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Yanzhou, he served as inspector outside the four gates of the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，移隨州。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou succeeded to the throne, Lingcong was transferred to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年，入為虎捷左第一軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiande, he entered the capital as commander-in-chief of the Tiger Swift Left First Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xiande era (955), he was recalled to the capital as commander-in-chief of the Tiger Swift Left First Army.

sentences.zh: 六年，兼領建州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he concurrently held the prefecture of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xiande, he was also made prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，出刺懷州。

translations.literal: When the Taizu ascended the throne, he went out as prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu of Song took the throne, Lingcong was sent out as prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 李筠叛，將親征，召三司張美餉兵食，美言河內密邇上黨，令琮日夜儲蓄以俟王師。

translations.literal: When Li Jing rebelled and the emperor was about to lead a personal campaign, he summoned Zhang Mei of the Three Bureaus to supply army provisions; Mei said that Henei lay close to Shangdang and that Lingcong should store supplies day and night to await the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing rebelled and the emperor prepared to lead the campaign in person, he summoned Zhang Mei of the Three Bureaus to provision the troops. Mei urged that Henei lay close to Shangdang and that Lingcong should stock supplies day and night against the arrival of the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，命授團練使。

translations.literal: The Taizu approved this and ordered that he be granted the post of regimental training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered that Lingcong be made regimental training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 執政言令琮方供億大軍，不可移他郡，故升懷州為團練，以令琮充使，又充先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said that Lingcong was then supplying a great army and could not be moved to another commandery; therefore Huaizhou was elevated to a regimental training prefecture, with Lingcong filling that post, and he was also made vanguard commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers argued that Lingcong was then provisioning the main army and could not be transferred elsewhere; Huaizhou was therefore elevated to a regimental training prefecture with Lingcong as commissioner, and he was also appointed vanguard commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 澤、潞平，為昭義兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: When Ze and Lu were pacified, he became military superintendent of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: After Ze and Lu were pacified, he was made military superintendent of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 逾年被疾，詔許歸郡。

translations.literal: After more than a year he fell ill, and an edict permitted him to return to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he fell ill, and the court permitted him to return to his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande, he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiande (963), he died at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚憐之，錄其子延恩為殿直。

translations.literal: The Taizu pitied him deeply and enrolled his son Yan'en as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and enrolled his son Yan'en as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 杜漢徽

translations.literal: Du Hanhui
translations.idiomatic: Du Hanhui

sentences.zh: 杜漢徽，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Du Hanhui, a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hanhui was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父阿孫，為太原威勝軍使。

translations.literal: His father A'sun served as commissioner of the Weisheng Army at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father A'sun was commissioner of the Weisheng Army at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 漢徽有膂力，善騎射，年十七，仕後唐武皇為廳直隊長。

translations.literal: Hanhu had great physical strength and excelled at mounted archery; at seventeen he entered the service of the Martial Emperor of Later Tang as captain of the hall attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Hanhu was powerfully built and skilled in horsemanship and archery. At seventeen he entered the service of the Martial Emperor of Later Tang as captain of the hall attendants.

sentences.zh: 天成中，累遷護聖軍使。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, he was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Imperial Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era he rose to command the Imperial Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 晉天福六年，與慕容鄴等討安州李金全，生禽指揮使孫厚，以功遷興順指揮使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu of Jin, with Murong Ye and others he campaigned against Li Jinquan of Anzhou, capturing alive the commander Sun Hou; for this merit he was promoted to commander of the Xingshun Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Tianfu era of Later Jin (941), he joined Murong Ye and others in the campaign against Li Jinquan of Anzhou and took the commander Sun Hou alive. For this merit he was promoted to commander of the Xingshun Army.

sentences.zh: 八年，從征鎮州安重榮，改護聖指揮使，贈阿孫為左讚善大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he followed the campaign against An Chongrong of Zhenzhou, was changed to commander of the Imperial Guard, and A'sun was posthumously granted the title of Left Palatine Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took part in the campaign against An Chongrong of Zhenzhou and was made commander of the Imperial Guard; his father A'sun was posthumously granted the title of Left Palatine Counselor.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，以所部戍深州，破契丹於樂壽，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, with his command he garrisoned Shenzhou, defeated the Khitan at Leshou, and killed and captured a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun (945) he garrisoned Shenzhou with his troops, defeated the Khitan at Leshou, and killed or captured a great number of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 漢初，從高行周討杜重威於鄴，屢為流矢所中，身被重創，猶力戰，觀者壯之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, he followed Gao Xingzhou in campaigning against Du Chongwei at Ye, was repeatedly struck by stray arrows, suffered grave wounds, yet still fought fiercely; onlookers admired his valor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Han he followed Gao Xingzhou against Du Chongwei at Ye. He was hit repeatedly by stray arrows and bore grave wounds, yet kept fighting; those who watched were awed by his courage.

sentences.zh: 又率所部戍鎮州，破契丹於靈壽，獲車馬甚眾。

translations.literal: Again he led his command to garrison Zhenzhou, defeated the Khitan at Lingshou, and captured a great number of carts and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops to garrison Zhenzhou, defeated the Khitan at Lingshou, and seized a great quantity of carts and horses.

sentences.zh: 周世宗征劉崇，漢徽有戰功，補龍捷左第五軍都虞候，移所部屯安平縣，破契丹於縣南，獲器甲車帳，遷本軍左第四軍都虞候。

translations.literal: When Shizong of Zhou campaigned against Liu Chong, Hanhui had military merit; he was appointed deputy commander of the Dragon Swift Left Fifth Army, moved his command to garrison Anping County, defeated the Khitan south of the county, captured armor, carts, and tents, and was promoted to deputy commander of the Left Fourth Army of that corps.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Liu Chong, Hanhui distinguished himself. He was made deputy commander of the Dragon Swift Left Fifth Army and stationed his troops at Anping County, where he defeated the Khitan south of the county and seized armor, wagons, and tents. He was then promoted to deputy commander of the Left Fourth Army of the same corps.

sentences.zh: 宋初，補本軍都校，領茂州刺史，改領潮州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was appointed colonel of his army, held the prefecture of Maozhou, and was then changed to hold Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was made colonel of his army and prefect of Maozhou, then transferred to Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 從平李筠，又從平李重進，錄功居多。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Li Jing and again in the pacification of Li Chongjin, and in recording merit he ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the suppression of Li Jing and then of Li Chongjin, and his recorded merit ranked among the highest.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，出為天長軍使，移雄武軍使、知屯田事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, he went out as commissioner of the Tianchang Army, then was transferred to commissioner of the Xiongwu Army and charged with field administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong (962) he was sent out as commissioner of the Tianchang Army, then transferred to commissioner of the Xiongwu Army with responsibility for field administration.

sentences.zh: 是冬，被病，即以符印授通判宋鸞，請告歸京。

translations.literal: That winter he fell ill, immediately handed his seal and credentials to the vice prefect Song Luan, and requested leave to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he fell ill, handed his seal and credentials at once to the vice prefect Song Luan, and asked leave to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 家人勸其求醫藥，漢徽笑曰：「我在戎行四十年，大小百餘戰，不死幸矣，安用藥為？」

translations.literal: His family urged him to seek medicine; Hanhui smiled and said, "I have been in the army forty years and fought in more than a hundred engagements large and small; that I have not died is already fortunate—what use is medicine?"
translations.idiomatic: His family urged him to seek medical treatment. Hanhui smiled and said, "I have spent forty years in the army and fought in more than a hundred battles, great and small. That I have not died is already good fortune—what need have I of medicine?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 張廷翰

translations.literal: Zhang Tinghan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghan

sentences.zh: 張廷翰，冀州信都人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinghan, a native of Xindu in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghan was a native of Xindu in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 父慎圖，仕周為兵部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Shentu served Zhou as a director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shentu served the Zhou dynasty as a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 廷翰少慷慨，有智略，善騎射。

translations.literal: Tinghan from youth was magnanimous, possessed strategy, and excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tinghan was open-handed and resourceful, and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，冀州刺史張建武召補牙校，其後刺史李冲署為本州牢城軍校。

translations.literal: During Tianfu of Jin, the Jizhou prefect Zhang Jianwu summoned him to fill a yamen staff post; afterward the prefect Li Chong appointed him garrison commander of the prefecture's prison-city force.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Later Jin, the prefect of Jizhou, Zhang Jianwu, recruited him to his staff; his successor Li Chong then appointed him commander of the prefecture's prison-city garrison.

sentences.zh: 契丹入中原，署其黨何行通為刺史，契丹主道殂，州人共殺行通，推廷翰知州事。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the Central Plains, they installed their partisan He Xingtong as prefect; when the Khitan ruler died on the road, the people of the prefecture together killed Xingtong and urged Tinghan to manage prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered the Central Plains they installed their partisan He Xingtong as prefect. After the Khitan ruler died on the march, the people of the prefecture killed Xingtong together and pressed Tinghan to take charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 漢初，就拜刺史，廷翰盡捕殺行通者戮於市。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he was directly appointed prefect; Tinghan arrested all who had killed Xingtong and executed them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Han he was confirmed as prefect. Tinghan arrested everyone who had taken part in killing Xingtong and had them executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 為政寬厚簡易，民甚愛之。

translations.literal: His governance was lenient, generous, and simple, and the people greatly loved him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and unpretentious, and the people held him in great affection.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，召赴闕，周祖見其貌魁偉，謂樞密使王峻曰：「冀州近邊，雖更擇人，亦無踰廷翰者。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou he was summoned to court; the Zhou founder, seeing his imposing stature, said to the Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Jun, "Jizhou lies on the frontier; though another man were chosen, none would surpass Tinghan."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun era he was summoned to court. The Zhou founder, struck by his imposing stature, told the commissioner of military affairs Wang Jun, "Jizhou lies on the frontier. Even if we chose someone else, no one would surpass Tinghan."

sentences.zh: 即日遣還。

translations.literal: That same day he was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was sent back.

sentences.zh: 在郡八年，契丹將高牟翰數擾邊，皆為廷翰擊走。

translations.literal: During eight years in the commandery, the Khitan general Gao Mouhan repeatedly harassed the border, and on each occasion Tinghan drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: During eight years in office the Khitan general Gao Mouhan raided the border repeatedly, and each time Tinghan repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 廷翰家富於財，歲遣人齎金帛北入市善馬，常得數百匹，貢獻外悉遺貴近，甚獲美譽。

translations.literal: Tinghan's household was rich in wealth; each year he sent men bearing gold and silks north into the markets to buy fine horses, regularly obtaining several hundred head; apart from what he presented as tribute, he gave all to the eminent and those close at court, and thereby won great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghan's family was wealthy. Each year he sent agents north with gold and silks to buy fine horses in the markets, regularly obtaining several hundred head. Aside from what he presented as tribute, he gave the rest to eminent officials and those close to the throne, and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，歷棣、海、沂三州團練使，屢率兵敗淮人，移萊州。

translations.literal: During Xiande he successively held the regimental training commissionerships of Di, Hai, and Yi, repeatedly led troops to defeat the Huai region forces, and was transferred to Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era he served in turn as regimental training commissioner of Di, Hai, and Yi, led troops repeatedly to defeat the Huai armies, and was then transferred to Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，又歷冀、亳二州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he again successively held Ji and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he served in turn at Ji and Bo.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Qiande (964) at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 吳虔裕

translations.literal: Wu Qianyu
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qianyu

sentences.zh: 周祖討三叛，以虔裕為河中行營都監，率護聖諸軍五千以往。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned against the Three Rebels, he made Qianyu overall supervisor of the Hezhong field headquarters, leading five thousand men of the Imperial Guard armies thither.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder campaigned against the Three Rebels, he appointed Qianyu overall supervisor of the Hezhong field headquarters and led five thousand Imperial Guard troops there.

sentences.zh: 李守貞出兵五千餘，設梯橋，分五路於長連城西北以禦周祖。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen sent out more than five thousand troops, set up scaling bridges, and divided into five routes northwest of Changliancheng to resist the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen sent out more than five thousand men, erected scaling bridges, and deployed five columns northwest of Changliancheng to oppose the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 周祖令虔裕率大軍橫擊之，蒲人敗走，奪其梯橋，殺傷大半。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder ordered Qianyu to lead the main force in a flanking strike; the men of Pu were defeated and fled, their scaling bridges were seized, and more than half were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder ordered Qianyu to strike them with the main force from the flank. The defenders of Pu were routed, their scaling bridges were captured, and more than half were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜襲衣、玉帶。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted court robes and a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was rewarded with court robes and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 會樞密使楊邠上言求解職，隱帝遣人諭邠曰：「樞機之任，非卿不可，卿何聽間離而為此請耶？」

translations.literal: It happened that the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yang Bin memorialized requesting to resign his post; the Hidden Emperor sent someone to instruct Bin, saying, "The charge of the pivot is indispensable to you—why heed alienation and make this request?"
translations.idiomatic: At this time the commissioner of military affairs Yang Bin memorialized asking to resign. Emperor Yin sent a messenger to tell him, "The pivot of state affairs cannot do without you. Why heed those who would drive us apart and make such a request?"

sentences.zh: 使至而虔裕在坐，即颺言曰：「機要重地，非可久處，俾後來者迭居可也。」

translations.literal: When the messenger arrived, Qianyu was present at the session and immediately spoke aloud, saying, "This weighty post of vital secrets is not a place to remain long; it is fitting that those who come later should take turns holding it."
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger arrived, Qianyu was in attendance and spoke up at once: "Such a weighty post of state secrets is no place to linger. It is only right that those who come after should take turns in it."

sentences.zh: 使還以白帝，帝怒，出虔裕為鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: When the messenger returned and reported this to the emperor, the emperor was angry and sent Qianyu out as defensive commissioner of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger returned and reported this, the emperor was furious and sent Qianyu out as defensive commissioner of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末誅大臣，急詔入朝，命將兵守澶州。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou, when great ministers were executed, an urgent edict summoned him to court and ordered him to command troops guarding Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qianyou era, when great ministers were put to death, an urgent edict recalled him to court and ordered him to command troops at Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及留子陂戰敗，遂降周祖。

translations.literal: When the battle at Liuzi Slope was lost, he thereupon surrendered to the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Liuzi Slope he surrendered to the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，遣還，賜以襲衣、玉帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was sent back and granted court robes, a jade belt, and a saddled horse.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he was sent back and rewarded with court robes, a jade belt, and a saddled horse.

sentences.zh: 從周祖討慕容彥超，破之。

translations.literal: He followed the Zhou founder in campaigning against Murong Yanchao and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Zhou founder against Murong Yanchao and helped defeat him.

sentences.zh: 改汝州防禦使，歷右衛、左金吾衛二大將軍兼街仗使。

translations.literal: He was changed to defensive commissioner of Ruzhou, and successively served as grand general of the Right Guard and Left Golden Crow Guard, concurrently street guard commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made defensive commissioner of Ruzhou, then served in turn as grand general of the Right Guard and Left Golden Crow Guard, concurrently as street guard commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，遷右千牛衛上將軍，仍判左街仗事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, he was promoted to upper general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, still overseeing left street guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo (981) he was promoted to upper general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard while continuing to oversee left street guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 虔裕掌金吾三十餘年，端拱初卒，年八十八，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Qianyu held charge of the Golden Crow Guard for more than thirty years; at the beginning of Duangong he died, aged eighty-eight, and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyu held command of the Golden Crow Guard for more than thirty years. He died early in the Duangong era (988) at the age of eighty-eight and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 虔裕性簡率，言多輕肆。

translations.literal: Qianyu's nature was plain and direct, and his speech was often reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyu was plain-spoken by nature and often spoke rashly.

sentences.zh: 右金吾上將軍王彥超告老，虔裕語人曰：「我縱僵仆殿階下，斷不學王彥超七十致仕。」

translations.literal: When the upper general of the Right Golden Crow Guard Wang Yanchao reported old age and requested retirement, Qianyu said to others, "Even if I stiffen and fall below the palace steps, I will never imitate Wang Yanchao in retiring at seventy."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yanchao, upper general of the Right Golden Crow Guard, petitioned to retire on account of age, Qianyu told others, "Even if I stiffen and fall on the palace steps, I will never follow Wang Yanchao's example of retiring at seventy."

sentences.zh: 人傳笑之。

translations.literal: People spread the story and laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: The remark was passed around and much laughed at.

sentences.zh: 每朝會及從遊宴，太宗憐其壽高，常慰撫之。

translations.literal: At every court assembly and when he followed in excursions and banquets, Taizong pitied his great age and often comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies and on excursions and banquets, Emperor Taizong, mindful of his great age, often comforted him.

sentences.zh: 子延彬，至儀鸞副使。

translations.literal: His son Yanbin rose to deputy commissioner of the Ceremonial Phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanbin rose to deputy commissioner of the Ceremonial Phoenix Guard.

sentences.zh: 延彬子仁美，至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Yanbin's son Renmei rose to honorary rank of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbin's son Renmei rose to honorary rank in the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 蔡審廷

translations.literal: Cai Shenting
translations.idiomatic: Cai Shenting

sentences.zh: 蔡審廷，磁州武安人。

translations.literal: Cai Shenting, a native of Wu'an in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Shenting was a native of Wu'an in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖凝，邢州別駕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ning was vice prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ning was vice prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖綰，武安遠城三冶使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wan was commissioner of the three smelteries of Yuancheng in Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wan was commissioner of the three smelteries at Yuancheng in Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 父顒，洺州長史。

translations.literal: His father Yong was senior recorder of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong was senior recorder of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 審廷少能騎射，晉初，應募補護聖散都頭。

translations.literal: Shenting from youth could ride and shoot; at the beginning of Jin he answered the recruitment and was appointed a scattered company head of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shenting was skilled in horsemanship and archery. Early in Later Jin he enlisted and was appointed a scattered company head in the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，擢為殿前散員，轉鐵騎副兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou he was promoted to a scattered attendant before the throne, then transferred to deputy horse-and-arms commissioner of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiande era of Later Zhou he was promoted to a scattered attendant before the throne, then made deputy horse-and-arms commissioner of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從世宗戰高平有功，遷軍使。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong in the battle at Gaoping with merit and was promoted to army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Gaoping under Emperor Shizong with distinction and was promoted to army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太祖為殿前都點檢，從世宗征淮南，審廷隸麾下，預戰紫金山，改副指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Taizu was overall inspector of the Palace Front, he followed Shizong in the Huainan campaign; Shenting served under his command, took part in the battle at Purple Gold Mountain, and was changed to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Taizu was overall inspector of the Palace Front, Shenting served under him in Emperor Shizong's Huainan campaign, fought at Purple Gold Mountain, and was made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 宋初，授殿前散都頭指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was appointed commander of the scattered company heads before the throne in the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was appointed commander of the scattered company heads of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 從征李筠，攻澤州先登，為飛石傷足，帝賜以良藥、美酒。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Li Jing, was first to scale the walls in the assault on Zezhou, was wounded in the foot by a flying stone, and the emperor granted him fine medicine and good wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Jing he was first over the wall at Zezhou and was struck in the foot by a catapult stone. The emperor rewarded him with fine medicine and wine.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還京，幸其官署問之，賜齎甚厚。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, the emperor visited his official quarters to inquire after him and granted gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, he visited Shenting at his quarters to inquire after him and bestowed lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 尋轉內殿直都虞候，俄改伴飯都指揮使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to deputy commander of the Inner Hall Direct, and soon changed to commander of the Companion Meal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made deputy commander of the Inner Hall Direct Guard, then commander of the Companion Meal Guard.

sentences.zh: 建隆中，領富州刺史兼內外馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: During Jianlong he held the prefecture of Fuzhou and concurrently served as deputy overall army head of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianlong era he was prefect of Fuzhou and concurrently deputy overall commander of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，授冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, he was appointed Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande he was appointed prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 征太原時，為北面步軍都指揮使，屯兵易州。

translations.literal: During the Taiyuan campaign, he was commander-in-chief of the northern foot armies and stationed troops at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan campaign he was commander-in-chief of the northern infantry and stationed his troops at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 審廷訓練士卒甚整，太祖過鎮陽，見於行在所，賜名馬、寶劍，命為鎮州兵馬都鈐轄。

translations.literal: Shenting trained his soldiers with great discipline; when the Taizu passed through Zhenyang, he received him at the mobile headquarters, granted him a famous horse and a treasured sword, and appointed him overall military superintendent of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenting drilled his troops to a high standard. When the emperor passed through Zhenyang, he received Shenting at the field headquarters, gave him a fine horse and a treasured sword, and appointed him overall military superintendent of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Kaibao (975) at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 周廣，字大均，其先應州神武川人。

translations.literal: Zhou Guang, style name Dajun, his ancestors were people of Shenwu River in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Guang, whose style was Dajun, came from a family of Shenwu River in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父密，事晉，歷鄜、延、晉三鎮節度使。

translations.literal: His father Mi served Jin and successively held the military governorships of Fu, Yan, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mi served Later Jin and in turn was military governor of Fu, Yan, and Jin.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，至太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, he reached Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he rose to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

sentences.zh: 廣幼從其父為牙校。

translations.literal: Guang from youth followed his father as a yamen staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Guang served on his father's personal staff.

sentences.zh: 漢初，授供奉官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, he was appointed a tribute attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Han he was appointed a tribute attendant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢左千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 周祖命將討慕容彥超於兗州，以廣為行營都監。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder ordered generals to campaign against Murong Yanchao at Yanzhou and made Guang overall supervisor of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder ordered a campaign against Murong Yanchao at Yanzhou, he made Guang overall supervisor of the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 賊平，錄功遷右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, his merit was recorded and he was promoted to general of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were subdued, his merit was recorded and he was promoted to general of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 俄改右神武將軍，充鎮淮軍兵馬都監。

translations.literal: Shortly he was changed to general of the Right Divine Martial Guard and filled the post of overall military supervisor of the Zhenhuai Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general of the Right Divine Martial Guard and overall military supervisor of the Zhenhuai Army.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征淮南。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong in the Huainan campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Shizong on the Huainan campaign.

sentences.zh: 既得江北數州，即命廣勞來安集，民甚德之。

translations.literal: Once several prefectures north of the river were taken, he was immediately ordered to comfort the people and settle them; the people greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: After several prefectures north of the Yangzi were secured, Guang was sent to comfort the people and restore order, and they held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 因領常州刺史兼內外馬步軍都軍頭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he held the prefecture of Changzhou and concurrently served as overall army head of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made prefect of Changzhou and concurrently overall commander of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，改眉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, he was changed to Prefect of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Huainan was pacified, he was transferred to Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，授隰州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was appointed Prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was appointed prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，遷潘州團練使，令訓練雄武諸營。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, he was transferred to regimental training commissioner of Panzhou and ordered to train the camps of the Xiongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiande (965) he was made regimental training commissioner of Panzhou and charged with drilling the Xiongwu camps.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，從征太原，為攻城樓櫓戰棹都部署，師還，加內外馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, he followed the Taiyuan campaign as overall deployer of siege towers, mantlets, and war boats; when the army returned, he was added as deputy overall army head of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao (969) he joined the Taiyuan campaign as overall commander of siege works and war boats. When the army returned, he was promoted to deputy overall commander of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 六年，改右屯衛大將軍，領郡如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was changed to grand general of the Right Garrison Guard, holding his commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made grand general of the Right Garrison Guard while retaining his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taiping Xingguo (977).

sentences.zh: 張勳，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun, a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 晉開運中，事留守景延廣為典客，延廣表為供奉官。

translations.literal: During Kaiyun of Jin, he served the regent Jing Yanguang as protocol officer; Yanguang memorialized him as a tribute attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun era of Later Jin he served the regent Jing Yanguang as protocol officer, and Yanguang recommended him for appointment as a tribute attendant.

sentences.zh: 周世宗將征淮南，以勳為申州緣淮巡檢。

translations.literal: When Shizong of Zhou was about to campaign against Huainan, he made Xun Huai-river inspection commissioner along the border of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong prepared to campaign against Huainan, he appointed Xun inspection commissioner along the Huai on the Shenzhou frontier.

sentences.zh: 因採光州機事聞於朝廷，即命勳率兵同討平之，遂監光州軍，充內外巡檢。

translations.literal: Because he gathered intelligence on Guangzhou affairs and reported to court, he was immediately ordered to lead troops jointly to suppress and pacify it; he then supervised the Guangzhou army and filled the post of inner and outer inspector.
translations.idiomatic: After he reported intelligence on Guangzhou to the court, he was ordered to lead troops to suppress the disturbance. He then supervised the Guangzhou garrison and served as inner and outer inspector.

sentences.zh: 後攻黃州，敗吳人於麻城，復破柏業山砦，目中流矢。

translations.literal: Later he attacked Huangzhou, defeated Wu forces at Macheng, again stormed the stockade at Boye Mountain, and was struck in the eye by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: He later attacked Huangzhou, defeated Wu troops at Macheng, and stormed the stockade at Boye Mountain, where a stray arrow struck him in the eye.

sentences.zh: 遷內園副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy commissioner of the Inner Park.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commissioner of the Inner Park.

sentences.zh: 及征瀛、莫，以為霸州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Ying and Mo, he was made overall military supervisor of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Ying and Mo, he was made overall military supervisor of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 初，征李筠，勳從石守信董前軍，拔大會砦，及敗筠眾於太行，破澤州，皆預有功。

translations.literal: At first, in the campaign against Li Jing, Xun followed Shi Shouxin in directing the vanguard, captured the Dahui stockade, and when Jing's forces were defeated in the Taihang and Zezhou was taken, he shared in the merit on each occasion.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Jing, Xun served under Shi Shouxin in the vanguard, captured the Dahui stockade, and shared in the victories over Li Jing's army in the Taihang and at Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖還京，命權知許州。

translations.literal: When the Taizu returned to the capital, he was ordered to act as prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Xun was appointed acting prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李重進叛，又詔與石守信、李處耘先率兵進討。

translations.literal: Before long, when Li Chongjin rebelled, an edict again ordered him with Shi Shouxin and Li Chuyun to lead troops forward first in the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when Li Chongjin rebelled, he was again ordered with Shi Shouxin and Li Chuyun to lead the advance against him.

sentences.zh: 拔揚州，以勳為兵馬都監，遷氈毯使。

translations.literal: When Yangzhou was taken, Xun was made military supervisor and promoted to commissioner of felts and rugs.
translations.idiomatic: After Yangzhou was captured, Xun was made military supervisor and promoted to commissioner of felts and rugs.

sentences.zh: 討朗陵，充前軍兵馬都監。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Langling, he served as vanguard military supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Langling he served as vanguard military supervisor.

sentences.zh: 荊湖平，以功就拜衡州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jinghu was pacified, for his merit he was directly appointed Prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinghu was pacified, his merit earned him appointment as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，克郴州及桂陽監，以勳為刺史兼監使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, when Chenzhou and the Guiyang Directorate were taken, Xun was made prefect and concurrently director commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande, after Chenzhou and the Guiyang salt directorate were captured, Xun was made prefect and concurrently director commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，代歸，至揚州卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when relieved and returning, he died at Yangzhou, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, while returning after being relieved of his post, he died at Yangzhou at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚憐之，錄其子廷敏為殿直。

translations.literal: The Taizu pitied him deeply and enrolled his son Tingmin as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and enrolled his son Tingmin as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 勳性殘忍好殺，每攻破城邑，但揚言曰「且斬」，頗有橫罹鋒刃者。

translations.literal: Xun's nature was cruel and bloodthirsty; whenever he stormed a walled city he would only proclaim, "For now, execute," and many innocents perished by the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was cruel and bloodthirsty. Whenever he took a city he would announce only, "Execute for now," and many who had done no wrong fell to the sword.

sentences.zh: 將赴衡州，州民皆涕泣相謂曰：「『張且斬』至矣，吾輩何以安乎！」

translations.literal: When he was about to proceed to Hengzhou, the people of the prefecture all wept and said to one another, "'Zhang Execute-for-Now' is coming—how can we be at peace!"
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to take up his post at Hengzhou, the people wept and said to one another, "'Zhang Execute-for-Now' is coming—how shall we live in peace?"

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，再使高麗，遷左驍衛大將軍，護秦州屯兵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, he was again sent as envoy to Goryeo, was promoted to grand general of the Left Valiant Guard, and guarded the garrison troops at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong (962) he was again sent as envoy to Goryeo, promoted to grand general of the Left Valiant Guard, and put in charge of the garrison at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 西人犯邊，曦率所領擊破之，斬渠帥十三人。

translations.literal: When western tribes raided the border, Xi led his command to defeat them and beheaded thirteen chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: When western tribes raided the frontier, Xi led his troops to defeat them and beheaded thirteen chieftains.

sentences.zh: 太祖征晉，曦領兵二千人自澤、潞除道至太原，壅汾水灌其城，又益兵千人，部攻遼州。

translations.literal: When the Taizu campaigned against Jin, Xi led two thousand men by a cleared route from Ze and Lu to Taiyuan, dammed the Fen River to flood the city, added another thousand troops, and directed the assault on Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's campaign against Northern Han, Xi led two thousand men by a cleared route from Ze and Lu to Taiyuan, dammed the Fen to flood the city, reinforced his force by a thousand, and directed the attack on Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 俄知雄州，代，為潭州鈐轄。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made prefect of Xiongzhou; when relieved, he became military superintendent of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Xiongzhou, and when relieved of that post was appointed military superintendent of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，領兵敗南唐軍二千餘於袁州，平梅山、板倉諸洞蠻寇，俘馘數千人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao, he led troops to defeat more than two thousand Southern Tang soldiers at Yuanzhou, pacified the Miao bandits of Meishan, Bancang, and other cave settlements, and captured or slew several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaibao (975) he defeated more than two thousand Southern Tang troops at Yuanzhou, pacified the tribal raiders of Meishan, Bancang, and other settlements, and took several thousand prisoners or heads.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，歷右神武、右羽林大將軍，連知孟、襄二州，遷領誠州刺史。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo, he successively served as grand general of the Right Divine Martial and Right Feathered Forest Guards, in succession governed Meng and Xiang, and was transferred to hold the prefecture of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era he served in turn as grand general of the Right Divine Martial and Right Feathered Forest Guards, governed Meng and Xiang in succession, and was transferred to Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，改知霸州兼部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, he was changed to govern Bazhou and concurrently serve as deployer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongxi (987) he was made prefect of Bazhou with concurrent authority as deployer.

sentences.zh: 會陳廷山謀以平戎軍叛入北邊，曦察知之，與侯延濟定計，禽廷山以獻。

translations.literal: It happened that Chen Tingshan plotted to rebel with Pingrong Army and defect to the northern border; Xi detected this, devised a plan with Hou Yanji, and captured Tingshan to present to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Tingshan plotted to rebel with the Pingrong garrison and defect to the northern tribes, Xi uncovered the scheme, worked out a plan with Hou Yanji, and captured Tingshan for presentation to the court.

sentences.zh: 錄其功，加領本州團練使、同知鎮州。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was additionally granted regimental training commissioner of his prefecture and concurrent administrator of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded and he was additionally made regimental training commissioner of his prefecture and concurrent administrator of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，移原州，遷右龍武軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, he was moved to Yuanzhou and promoted to grand general of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua (991) he was transferred to Yuanzhou and promoted to grand general of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 被病請告，詔特給全俸。

translations.literal: Stricken with illness, he requested leave; an edict specially granted him full salary.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill and asked for leave, the court specially granted him his full salary.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年七十四，賵賻加等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he died, aged seventy-four, and funeral gifts were granted above the usual grade.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year at the age of seventy-four, and funeral gifts were granted above the usual scale.

sentences.zh: 張藏英

translations.literal: Zhang Cangying
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cangying

sentences.zh: 張藏英，涿州范陽人，自言唐相嘉貞之後。

translations.literal: Zhang Cangying, a native of Fanyang in Zhuozhou, declared himself a descendant of the Tang chancellor Jia Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cangying was a native of Fanyang in Zhuozhou and claimed descent from the Tang chancellor Zhang Jiazhen.

sentences.zh: 唐末，舉族為賊孫居道所害。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, his entire clan was killed by the bandit Sun Judao.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tang dynasty his entire clan was slaughtered by the bandit Sun Judao.

sentences.zh: 藏英年十七，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Cangying was seventeen and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Cangying was seventeen and barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 後逢居道於豳州市，引佩刀刺之，不死，為吏所執。

translations.literal: Later he encountered Judao at Binzhou market, drew his belt dagger and stabbed him, but did not kill him, and was seized by officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later he met Judao at the market in Binzhou, drew his dagger, and stabbed him but failed to kill him, and was seized by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 節帥趙德鈞壯之，釋而不問，以補牙職。

translations.literal: The military governor Zhao Dejun admired his spirit, released him without punishment, and appointed him to a yamen post.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor Zhao Dejun admired his courage, released him without punishment, and gave him a post on his staff.

sentences.zh: 藏英後聞居道避地關南，乃求為關南都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Cangying later heard that Judao had taken refuge in Guannan and therefore requested appointment as Guannan metropolitan inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Learning later that Judao had fled to Guannan, Cangying sought appointment as metropolitan inspection commissioner of Guannan.

sentences.zh: 至則微服攜鐵楇，匿居道舍側，伺其出，擊之仆於地，齧其耳噉之，遂禽歸。

translations.literal: On arrival he went in disguise carrying an iron club, hid beside Judao's dwelling, waited for him to come out, struck him down, bit off his ear and devoured it, and then captured him and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he went in disguise with an iron club, hid beside Judao's house, and when Judao came out struck him down, bit off his ear and ate it, then took him captive.

sentences.zh: 設父母位，陳酒肴，縛居道於前，號泣鞭之，臠其肉，經三日，刳其心以祭。

translations.literal: He set up places for his parents, laid out wine and food, bound Judao before them, wept and whipped him, sliced his flesh, and after three days cut out his heart as an offering.
translations.idiomatic: He set up memorial tablets for his parents, spread wine and food, bound Judao before them, wept as he whipped him, carved flesh from his body, and after three days cut out his heart as an offering.

sentences.zh: 即詣官首服，官為上請而釋之。

translations.literal: He then went to the authorities to confess; the officials memorialized upward and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He then surrendered to the authorities, who memorialized the court and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 燕、薊間目為「報讐張孝子」。

translations.literal: Between Yan and Ji he was known as "Filial Zhang Who Avenged His Kin."
translations.idiomatic: Between Yan and Ji he was known as "Filial Zhang the Avenger."

sentences.zh: 契丹用為盧䑓軍使兼榷鹽制置使，領坊州刺史。

translations.literal: The Khitan employed him as commissioner of the Lu'an Army and concurrently salt monopoly superintendent, holding the prefecture of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan appointed him commissioner of the Lu'an Army and salt monopoly superintendent, with the prefecture of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 周廣順三年，率內外親屬並所部兵千餘人，及煮鹽戶長幼七千餘口，牛馬萬計，舟數百艘，航海歸周。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, he led more than a thousand kinsmen inside and outside his clan together with troops under his command, and more than seven thousand persons young and old of salt-boiling households, tens of thousands of cattle and horses, and several hundred boats, returning to Zhou by sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangshun (953) he led more than a thousand kinsmen and troops under his command, more than seven thousand salt-workers and their families, tens of thousands of cattle and horses, and several hundred boats, and returned to Zhou by sea.

sentences.zh: 至滄州，刺史李暉以聞。

translations.literal: On reaching Cangzhou, the prefect Li Hui reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Cangzhou, Prefect Li Hui reported his arrival to the court.

sentences.zh: 周祖頗疑之，令館於封禪寺，俄賜襲衣、銀帶、錢十萬、絹百匹、銀器、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder was quite suspicious and had him lodged at Fengchan Temple; shortly he was granted court robes, a silver belt, one hundred thousand in cash, a hundred bolts of silk, silver vessels, and a saddled horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder was wary and had him lodged at Fengchan Temple, then soon rewarded him with court robes, a silver belt, one hundred thousand cash, a hundred bolts of silk, silver vessels, and a saddled horse.

sentences.zh: 數月，世宗即位，授德州刺史。

translations.literal: Several months later, when Shizong took the throne, he was appointed Prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, when Emperor Shizong took the throne, he was appointed prefect of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾召歸，對便殿，詢以備邊之策。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled, received in the informal hall, and questioned on strategies for border defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled, received in the informal hall, and questioned on border defense.

sentences.zh: 藏英請於深州李晏口置砦，及誘境上亡命者以隸軍，願為主將，得便宜討擊。

translations.literal: Cangying requested to build a stockade at Liyan Ford in Shenzhou and to entice fugitives on the border into army service; he wished to be the commanding general with discretionary authority to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Cangying asked to build a stockade at Liyan Ford in Shenzhou, recruit border fugitives into his force, and serve as commander with discretionary authority to attack.

sentences.zh: 世宗悉從之。

translations.literal: Shizong approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 以為緣邊招收都指揮使，賜名馬、金帶。

translations.literal: He was made frontier recruitment commander-in-chief and granted a famous horse and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was made frontier recruitment commander-in-chief and rewarded with a fine horse and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 藏英遂築城李晏口，累月，募得勁兵數千人。

translations.literal: Cangying thereupon built a fort at Liyan Ford; within months he recruited several thousand crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cangying then built a fort at Liyan Ford and within months recruited several thousand seasoned troops.

sentences.zh: 會遣鳳翔節度王彥超巡邊，為契丹所圍，藏英率新募兵馳往擊之，轉戰十餘里，契丹解去。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Yanchao, military governor of Fengxiang, was sent to patrol the border and was surrounded by Khitan; Cangying led his newly recruited troops in a rapid strike, fought for more than ten li, and the Khitan withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yanchao of Fengxiang was sent to patrol the border and was surrounded by Khitan forces, Cangying rushed his new recruits to the rescue, fought for more than ten li, and the Khitan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 改濮州刺史，仍領邊任。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of Puzhou, still holding his frontier duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Puzhou while retaining his frontier duties.

sentences.zh: 契丹將高牟翰以精騎數千擾邊，藏英逆擊於胡盧河北，自旦至晡，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: The Khitan general Gao Mouhan harassed the border with several thousand elite horsemen; Cangying met him north of the Hulu River and from dawn to dusk killed and wounded a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan general Gao Mouhan raided the border with several thousand elite horsemen. Cangying met him north of the Hulu River and from dawn to dusk killed and wounded a great many.

sentences.zh: 值暮收兵，契丹遁去。

translations.literal: At dusk he withdrew his troops and the Khitan fled.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he withdrew, and the Khitan fled.

sentences.zh: 後因領兵巡樂壽，契丹幽州驍將姚內斌偵知藏英兵少，以精騎二千陣於縣之北，藏英率麾下擊之，自辰及申，士皆殊死戰，內斌遂解去。

translations.literal: Later, while leading troops on patrol at Leshou, Yao Neibin, a fierce Khitan general of Youzhou, detected that Cangying had few troops and arrayed two thousand elite horsemen north of the county; Cangying led his men to attack from the hour chen to the hour shen, all fighting to the death, and Neibin then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while patrolling Leshou, he learned that Yao Neibin, a fierce Khitan general of Youzhou, had learned his force was small and drawn up two thousand elite horsemen north of the county. Cangying attacked from morning to mid-afternoon; his men fought to the death, and Neibin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 世宗降璽書褒美。

translations.literal: Shizong sent down an imperial letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent an imperial letter praising him.

sentences.zh: 征瓦橋關，為先鋒都指揮使，敗契丹騎數百於關北。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Wagong Pass, he was vanguard commander-in-chief and defeated several hundred Khitan horsemen north of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Wagong Pass he served as vanguard commander-in-chief and defeated several hundred Khitan horsemen north of the pass.

sentences.zh: 下固安縣，又改關南排陣使。

translations.literal: He took Gu'an County and was again changed to Guannan battle-array commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Gu'an County and was made Guannan battle-array commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷瀛州團練使，並護關南軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was transferred to regimental training commissioner of Yingzhou and concurrently guarded the Guannan army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was made regimental training commissioner of Yingzhou and put in charge of the Guannan army.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，卒於治所，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, he died at his seat of government, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post in the third year of Jianlong (962) at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 孫鑒，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Jian has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Jian has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 陸萬友

translations.literal: Lu Wanyou
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wanyou

sentences.zh: 陸萬友，蔚州靈丘人。

translations.literal: Lu Wanyou, a native of Lingqiu in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wanyou was a native of Lingqiu in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少隸太原為裨校。

translations.literal: From youth he was attached to Taiyuan as a deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served at Taiyuan as a deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 漢祖起義，擢為護聖指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Han founder rose in revolt, he was promoted to commander of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Han rose in revolt, he was promoted to commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，出為天雄軍馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor took the throne, he went out as commander-in-chief of the horse army of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yin took the throne, he was sent out as commander-in-chief of the Tianxiong cavalry.

sentences.zh: 周祖之起兵也，萬友預謀。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder raised his army, Wanyou took part in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder raised his army, Wanyou took part in the planning.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，擢為散員都指揮使，領獎州刺史。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Wanyou was promoted to commander of the scattered attendants and held the prefecture of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, Wanyou was promoted to commander of the scattered attendants and made prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，遷龍捷左第三軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, he was transferred to commander-in-chief of the Dragon Swift Left Third Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, he was made commander-in-chief of the Dragon Swift Left Third Army.

sentences.zh: 轉控鶴右廂都校、領虔州團練使，改虎捷右廂、領閬州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to colonel of the right wing of the Crane Control Guard and held the regimental training commissionership of Qianzhou, then changed to the Tiger Swift right wing and held the defensive commissionership of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made colonel of the right wing of the Crane Control Guard and regimental training commissioner of Qianzhou, then colonel of the Tiger Swift right wing and defensive commissioner of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，出為安州防禦使。

translations.literal: When the Gong Emperor succeeded, he went out as defensive commissioner of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, he was sent out as defensive commissioner of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，歷沂、蘄二州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he successively held the defensive commissionerships of Yi and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he served in turn as defensive commissioner of Yi and Qi.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，改汝州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande, he was changed to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande (966) he was transferred to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，討南唐，造舟於采石磯以濟師，命萬友守之。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, in the campaign against Southern Tang, boats were built at Caishi Ford to ferry the army, and Wanyou was ordered to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era, in the campaign against Southern Tang, boats were built at Caishi Ford to ferry the army, and Wanyou was ordered to guard them.

sentences.zh: 江南平，為和州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he became defensive commissioner of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified, he was made defensive commissioner of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，以為晉、絳等州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded, he was made metropolitan inspection commissioner of Jin, Jiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong succeeded, he was made metropolitan inspection commissioner of Jin, Jiang, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 帝征太原，克汾、石二州，以萬友為石州都巡檢使，俄兼知石州，移巡警鳳翔、秦、隴。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Taiyuan and took Fen and Shi, Wanyou was made metropolitan inspection commissioner of Shizhou, shortly also acting prefect of Shizhou, then transferred to patrol Fengxiang, Qin, and Long.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan campaign, after Fen and Shi were taken, Wanyou was made metropolitan inspection commissioner of Shizhou and soon also acting prefect; he was then transferred to patrol Fengxiang, Qin, and Long.

sentences.zh: 代歸，詔知瀛州，在郡二年，政務苟簡。

translations.literal: When relieved and returning, an edict appointed him to govern Yingzhou; during two years in the commandery his administration was perfunctory.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned after being relieved, he was appointed prefect of Yingzhou. During two years in office his administration was lax.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，改右監門衛大將軍，充河陰兵馬都監，逾年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, he was changed to grand general of the Right Gate Guard, filled the post of overall military supervisor of Heyin, and after more than a year died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi (985) he was made grand general of the Right Gate Guard and overall military supervisor of Heyin. He died a year later at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 萬友始業圬鏝，既貴達，不忘本，以銀為圬鏝器數十事示子孫。

translations.literal: Wanyou's first trade was plastering and troweling; once he had risen to eminence he did not forget his origins and had several dozen plastering tools made in silver to show his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyou had begun as a plasterer. After he rose to high rank he did not forget his origins and had several dozen plastering tools made in silver to show his descendants.

sentences.zh: 性猛暴，以武勇自任，所至無善政。

translations.literal: His nature was fierce and violent; he relied on martial valor, and wherever he went there was no good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce by nature, prided himself on martial prowess, and left good government nowhere he served.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其勳舊，恩遇不替，聘其次女為許王夫人。

translations.literal: Taizong, because he was an old merit-holder, did not diminish his favor; his second daughter was betrothed as consort to the Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was an old merit-holder, Emperor Taizong continued to favor him without decline and betrothed his second daughter to the Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 解暉，洺州臨洺人。

translations.literal: Jie Hui, a native of Linming in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Hui was a native of Linming in Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父珪，應募為州兵，後唐天成中，西征至劍門，沒於陣。

translations.literal: His father Gui answered the recruitment as a prefectural soldier; during Tiancheng of Later Tang, on the western campaign he reached Jianmen and perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui enlisted as a prefectural soldier. During the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, on a western campaign he reached Jianmen and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 暉少有勇力，以父死戎事，得隸兵籍。

translations.literal: Hui from youth had courage and strength; because his father died in military service, he was enrolled in the military registers.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Hui was strong and brave. Because his father had died in military service, he was enrolled in the army rolls.

sentences.zh: 戍雁門，與契丹接戰，斬首七級，獲酋長一人。

translations.literal: Garrisoned at Yanmen, he engaged the Khitan in battle, took seven heads, and captured one chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: While garrisoned at Yanmen he fought the Khitan, took seven heads, and captured one chieftain.

sentences.zh: 以功遷奉國軍隊長。

translations.literal: For this merit he was promoted to company leader of the Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was promoted to company leader in the Fengguo Army.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，安重榮反鎮州，因舉兵向闕。

translations.literal: During Tianfu of Jin, An Chongrong rebelled at Zhenzhou and thereupon raised troops toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Later Jin, An Chongrong rebelled at Zhenzhou and marched on the capital.

sentences.zh: 至宋城，晉師逆戰，大破之。

translations.literal: At Songcheng the Jin army met them in battle and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Songcheng the Jin army met them and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 暉募軍中壯士百餘人夜搗賊壘，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Hui recruited more than a hundred stalwarts from the army to storm the rebel camp by night, killing and capturing a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Hui recruited more than a hundred stalwarts from the army to raid the rebel camp by night, killing and capturing a great many.

sentences.zh: 暉頻中流失，而督戰自若，顏色不撓，以功遷本軍列校。

translations.literal: Hui was repeatedly struck by stray arrows, yet directed the battle with composure and his expression did not falter; for his merit he was promoted to company officer of his army.
translations.idiomatic: He was hit again and again by stray arrows, yet directed the battle calmly and without flinching, and was promoted to company officer in his corps for his merit.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，劉崇與契丹侵晉州，暉從都部署、樞密使王峻等往援之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, Liu Chong and the Khitan invaded Jinzhou; Hui followed the overall deployer and Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Jun and others to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun, when Liu Chong and the Khitan invaded Jinzhou, Hui followed the overall deployer Wang Jun and other commanders to the relief.

sentences.zh: 暉率敢死士三十餘，夜入契丹帳擊之，殺獲甚眾，遷本軍第五指揮使。

translations.literal: Hui led more than thirty dare-to-die soldiers, entered the Khitan camp by night to strike them, killed and captured a great multitude, and was promoted to fifth commander of his army.
translations.idiomatic: He led more than thirty volunteers in a night attack on the Khitan camp, killed and captured a great many, and was promoted to fifth commander of his army.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征淮南，率所部下黃州，禽刺史高弼，遷虎捷第一軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong in the Huainan campaign, led his command to take Huangzhou, captured the prefect Gao Bi, and was promoted to deputy commander of the Tiger Swift First Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Shizong's Huainan campaign he led his troops to Huangzhou, captured Prefect Gao Bi, and was made deputy commander of the Tiger Swift First Army.

sentences.zh: 宋初，步軍都軍頭，從征澤州，力戰，目中流矢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, as overall army head of the foot forces, he followed the Zezhou campaign, fought fiercely, and was struck in the eye by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty, as overall commander of the infantry, he fought at Zezhou with great ferocity and was struck in the eye by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 師還，策勳為內外馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his merit was assessed and he was made deputy overall army head of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, his merit earned him appointment as deputy overall commander of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，充湖廣道行營前軍戰棹都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, he served as commander-in-chief of war boats for the vanguard of the Huguang circuit field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong (963) he was made commander-in-chief of war boats for the vanguard of the Huguang field army.

sentences.zh: 潭州平，降璽書獎諭。

translations.literal: When Tanzhou was pacified, an imperial letter of commendation was sent down.
translations.idiomatic: When Tanzhou was pacified, the emperor sent him a letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 偽統軍黃從志據岳州，暉率舟師討平之，生禽從志及將校十四人，俘斬數千，溺死者眾。

translations.literal: The false overall commander Huang Congzhi held Yuezhou; Hui led a naval force to suppress and pacify it, captured Congzhi alive together with fourteen officers, took or slew several thousand, and many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel overall commander Huang Congzhi held Yuezhou. Hui led a fleet against him, took Congzhi alive with fourteen officers, killed or captured several thousand, and many drowned.

sentences.zh: 改控鶴右第二軍都指揮使，領高州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to commander-in-chief of the Crane Control Right Second Army and held the prefecture of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander-in-chief of the Crane Control Right Second Army and prefect of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年，詔領所部軍屯上黨，從李繼勳略太原。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiande, an edict ordered him to lead his army to garrison Shangdang and follow Li Jixun in raiding Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qiande (968) he was ordered to garrison Shangdang with his troops and join Li Jixun in raiding Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年，破太原軍於境上，斬首千餘級，獲馬三十匹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaibao, he defeated the Taiyuan army on the border, took more than a thousand heads, and seized thirty horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaibao (976) he defeated the Taiyuan army on the frontier, took more than a thousand heads, and seized thirty horses.

sentences.zh: 改均州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，詔於潞州北亂柳石圍中築城，名威勝軍，以暉為軍使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict ordered a fort built within the stone enclosure at Luanliu north of Luzhou, named the Weisheng Army, with Hui as army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo (977) he was ordered to build a fort at Luanliu north of Luzhou, named the Weisheng Army, and was made its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從征并州，與尚食使石彥贇率所部先下隆州，殺并州三百餘，禽招討使李詢等六人以獻於行在所，賜予有加。

translations.literal: He followed the Bingzhou campaign; with the Commissioner of Imperial Viands Shi Yanyun he led his command to take Longzhou first, killed more than three hundred men of Bingzhou, captured the pacification commissioner Li Xun and five others to present at the mobile headquarters, and received lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Bingzhou he and Commissioner of Imperial Viands Shi Yanyun led their troops to capture Longzhou first, killed more than three hundred defenders, and presented six captives including Pacification Commissioner Li Xun to the emperor's camp, receiving lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 復令與彥贇督戰士隸城西行營，分攻太原。

translations.literal: He was again ordered with Yanyun to supervise warriors attached to the western field camp outside the city and attack Taiyuan from that quarter.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered with Yanyun to command troops of the western field camp in the assault on Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 劉繼元降，太宗以太原宮女三人賜暉，俄以功遷本州團練使、知霸州。

translations.literal: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered, Taizong granted Hui three palace women of Taiyuan; shortly for his merit he was transferred to regimental training commissioner of his prefecture and acting prefect of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered, Emperor Taizong gave Hui three palace women from Taiyuan. Soon afterward his merit earned him promotion to regimental training commissioner of his prefecture and acting prefect of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，充雲、應、寰、朔、忻、代等州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, he filled the post of metropolitan inspection commissioner of Yun, Ying, Huan, Shuo, Xin, Dai, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi he was made metropolitan inspection commissioner of Yun, Ying, Huan, Shuo, Xin, Dai, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 三年，代歸本郡。

translations.literal: In the third year, when relieved, he returned to his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after being relieved, he returned to his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，被病，上章告老，改右千牛衛上將軍致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, stricken with illness, he memorialized to retire on account of age and was changed to upper general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard with retirement from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua (991), when he fell ill, he petitioned to retire and was made upper general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard with permission to leave office.

sentences.zh: 詔未至而卒，年八十。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the edict arrived, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 暉鷙猛木強，每受詔征伐，常身先之。

translations.literal: Hui was fierce, bold, and obstinate; whenever he received an edict for campaign, he always took the lead in person.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was fierce and unyielding. Whenever he received orders for a campaign, he always led from the front.

sentences.zh: 人所憚者，暉視之若甚易，由是頻立戰功，金創遍體。

translations.literal: What others dreaded, Hui treated as very easy; thereby he repeatedly won military merit, and wounds of bronze blades covered his body.
translations.idiomatic: What others feared he treated as easy work, and thus won repeated victories, his body covered with battle scars.

sentences.zh: 時稱驍將。

translations.literal: Of the time he was called a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: He was acclaimed as a fierce fighter.

sentences.zh: 子守顒，至內殿崇班、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His son Shouyong rose to honorary rank of the Inner Hall and palace gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouyong rose to honorary rank in the Inner Hall and served as a palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 李韜，河朔人。

translations.literal: Li Tao, a man of Heshuo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao was a native of the Hebei-Shandong region.

sentences.zh: 有勇力膽氣，善用槊，為禁軍隊長。

translations.literal: He had courage, strength, and daring, excelled at the spear, and was a company leader in the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was brave and daring, skilled with the spear, and served as a company leader in the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 周祖征三叛，韜從白文珂攻河中，兵傅其城。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned against the Three Rebels, Tao served under Bai Wenke in attacking Hezhong, the army pressing close to the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder campaigned against the Three Rebels, Tao followed Bai Wenke against Hezhong, pressing the army close to the walls.

sentences.zh: 文珂夜詣周祖議犒軍，留韜城下。

translations.literal: Wenke went by night to the Zhou founder to discuss rewarding the army, leaving Tao below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenke went by night to consult the Zhou founder about rewarding the troops, leaving Tao below the city.

sentences.zh: 時營柵未備，李守貞乘虛來襲，營中忽見火發，知賊聚至，惶怖失據。

translations.literal: At the time the camp palisade was not yet complete; Li Shouzhen seized the opportunity to raid; fire suddenly broke out in the camp, they knew the enemy had massed, and panic and loss of composure ensued.
translations.idiomatic: The camp fortifications were not yet complete when Li Shouzhen seized the chance to attack. Fire suddenly broke out in the camp; the men knew the enemy had come in force and panicked.

sentences.zh: 客省使閻晉卿率左右數十人，遇韜於月城側，謂韜曰：「事急矣，城中人悉被黃紙甲，為火光所照，色俱白，此殊易辨，奈軍士無鬥志何？”」

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Guest Bureau Yan Jinqing led several dozen attendants, met Tao beside the moon wall, and said to Tao, "The situation is urgent; all in the city wear yellow-paper armor, and lit by the fire their color all appears white—this is very easy to distinguish, but what of the soldiers having no fighting spirit?"
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of the Guest Bureau Yan Jinqing led several dozen men and met Tao beside the moon wall. He said, "The situation is desperate. Everyone in the city wears armor faced with yellow paper, which the firelight turns white—that is easy to tell apart. But what can we do when the soldiers have no heart to fight?"

sentences.zh: 韜憤怒曰：「豈有食君祿而不為國致死耶！」

translations.literal: Tao said in anger, "How can one eat the ruler's salary yet not die for the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Tao said angrily, "How can men who eat the ruler's salary refuse to die for the state!"

sentences.zh: 即援槊而進，軍中死士十餘輩隨韜犯賊鋒。

translations.literal: He immediately took up his spear and advanced, and more than a dozen dare-to-die men of the army followed Tao to strike the enemy's front.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his spear and charged forward, and more than a dozen volunteers followed him into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 蒲有猛將躍馬持戈擬韜，韜刺之，洞胸而墜。

translations.literal: A fierce general of Pu leaped on his horse and aimed his halberd at Tao; Tao stabbed him, pierced his chest, and he fell.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce Pu general spurred his horse and leveled his halberd at Tao. Tao ran him through the chest and brought him down.

sentences.zh: 又連殺數十人，蒲軍遂潰，因擊，大破之，守貞自是閉壘不敢出。

translations.literal: He then slew several tens more in succession; the Pu army thereupon collapsed, and pressing the attack he inflicted a great defeat; from then on Shouzhen closed his ramparts and did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: He killed dozens more in succession. The Pu army broke and was routed. From then on Shouzhen shut himself in his fort and did not dare come out.

sentences.zh: 俄驍將王三鐵降，城遂平，韜由此知名。

translations.literal: Shortly the fierce general Wang Santie surrendered, the city was thereupon pacified, and Tao became renowned from this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the fierce general Wang Santie surrendered, the city was taken, and Tao won fame from this exploit.

sentences.zh: 累遷軍校，出為趙州刺史，移慈州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted as an army officer, went out as Prefect of Zhaozhou, and was transferred to Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the army ranks, was sent out as prefect of Zhaozhou, and was transferred to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiande he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Qiande.

sentences.zh: 王晉卿

translations.literal: Wang Jinqing
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinqing

sentences.zh: 乾德中，為興州刺史。

translations.literal: During Qiande, he was Prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era he was prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，移漢州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時蜀初平，寇盜充斥，晉卿嚴武備，設方略，禽捕剪滅，靡有遺漏，自是雖劇賊無敢窺其境。
