translations.literal: At the time Shu had just been pacified and bandits filled the land; Jinqing tightened military preparations, devised stratagems, captured and exterminated them without omission, and from then on even fierce bandits did not dare peer into his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had just been pacified and bandits were everywhere. Jinqing strengthened defenses, laid plans, and hunted them down without exception, so that even the boldest raiders no longer dared enter his territory.

sentences.zh: 然以賄聞，太祖惜其才而不問。

translations.literal: Yet he became known for bribery; the Taizu valued his talent and did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for taking bribes, but the emperor valued his ability and did not investigate.

sentences.zh: 秩滿歸闕，以疾求頤養，改左監門衛將軍、奉朝請。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to court, requested convalescence on account of illness, and was changed to general of the Left Gate Guard and court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to court, asked leave to recuperate from illness, and was made general of the Left Gate Guard with the rank of court attendant.

sentences.zh: 貢重錦十匹、銀千兩以謝，詔不納，以其黷貨，愧之也。

translations.literal: He presented ten bolts of heavy brocade and a thousand taels of silver in thanks; an edict refused acceptance, shaming him for his corrupt goods.
translations.idiomatic: He offered ten bolts of heavy brocade and a thousand taels of silver in thanks. The court refused them, to shame him for his corruption.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔戍北邊，疆場清肅。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered him to garrison the northern border, and the frontier was cleared and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to the northern frontier, where he kept the border quiet.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，復授莫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, he was again appointed Prefect of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he was again appointed prefect of Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 在郡謹斥候，善撫循，士卒皆樂為之用，邊民安堵。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was strict in reconnaissance, good at comforting and guiding, the soldiers all gladly served under him, and the border people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: In office he maintained strict watch posts and treated men well; his soldiers served him gladly and the border people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 六年八月卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the sixth year at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 郭廷謂

translations.literal: Guo Tingwei
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tingwei

sentences.zh: 郭廷謂，字信臣，徐州彭城人。

translations.literal: Guo Tingwei, style name Xinchen, a native of Pengcheng in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tingwei, whose style was Xinchen, was a native of Pengcheng in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父全義，仕南唐為濠州觀察使。

translations.literal: His father Quanyi served Southern Tang as surveillance commissioner of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quanyi served Southern Tang as surveillance commissioner of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 廷謂幼好學，工書，善騎射。

translations.literal: Tingwei from youth loved learning, was skilled at calligraphy, and excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tingwei loved learning, was skilled at calligraphy, and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 補殿前承旨，改濠州中軍使，李景每令偵中朝機事入奏。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant before the throne, was changed to middle army commissioner of Haozhou, and Li Jing often ordered him to spy on affairs of the central court and report inward.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant before the throne, then made middle army commissioner of Haozhou, and Li Jing often sent him to spy on the central court and report back.

sentences.zh: 全義卒，擢莊宅使、濠州監軍。

translations.literal: When Quanyi died, he was promoted to commissioner of manorial estates and military supervisor of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanyi died, he was promoted to commissioner of manorial estates and military supervisor of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 周世宗攻淮右，南人屢敗，城中甚恐，廷謂與州將黃仁謙為固禦之計。

translations.literal: When Shizong of Zhou attacked the Huai west, the southerners were repeatedly defeated and fear in the city was great; Tingwei and the prefectural general Huang Renqian devised plans for solid defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong attacked the Huai west, the defenders suffered repeated defeats and the city was terrified. Tingwei and the prefectural commander Huang Renqian planned a stout defense.

sentences.zh: 周師遣諜以鐵券及其壘，廷謂拒之。

translations.literal: The Zhou army sent spies with iron tallies to their ramparts; Tingwei refused them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army sent spies with iron tallies to their ramparts, but Tingwei refused them.

sentences.zh: 城中負販之輩率不逞，廷謂慮其亡逸，籍置大寺，遣兵守之，給日食，俾製防城具，隨其所習，以故周師卒不得覘城中虛實。

translations.literal: The peddlers in the city were mostly unruly; Tingwei feared they would flee and scatter, registered and placed them in a great monastery, sent troops to guard them, supplied daily food, and had them make defensive equipment according to what each knew; for this reason the Zhou army in the end could not spy out the truth or falsehood within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The peddlers in the city were mostly unruly, and Tingwei feared they would slip away. He registered them in a great monastery, posted guards, fed them daily, and set them to making defensive gear according to their skills, so that the Zhou army could not learn the city's true condition.

sentences.zh: 周師為浮梁渦口，命張從恩、焦繼勳守之，廷謂語仁謙曰：「此濠、壽之患也。

translations.literal: The Zhou army built a pontoon bridge at Wokou; Zhang Cong'en and Jiao Jixun were ordered to guard it; Tingwei said to Renqian, "This is the trouble of Hao and Shou.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army built a pontoon bridge at Wokou and put Zhang Cong'en and Jiao Jixun in charge of it. Tingwei told Renqian, "This threatens Hao and Shou.

sentences.zh: 彼以騎士勝，故利於陸；

translations.literal: They prevail with cavalry, and therefore profit on land;
translations.idiomatic: They rely on cavalry and are strong on land;

sentences.zh: 我以舟師銳，故便於水。

translations.literal: we are sharp with naval forces, and therefore advantaged on water.
translations.idiomatic: we are strong on the water with our fleet.

sentences.zh: 今夏久雨，淮流泛溢，願假舟兵二千，斷其橋，屠其城，直抵壽春。」

translations.literal: This summer the rains have been long and the Huai overflows; I wish to borrow two thousand boat troops, cut their bridge, slaughter their fort, and go straight to Shouchun."
translations.idiomatic: This summer the rains have been heavy and the Huai is in flood. Lend me two thousand naval troops, and I will cut their bridge, destroy their fort, and strike straight for Shouchun."

sentences.zh: 仁謙初沮其議，不得已從之，即輕棹銜枚抵其橋，麾兵斷笮，悉焚之。

translations.literal: Renqian at first blocked his proposal, but had no choice but to agree; they immediately took light boats with gags in the men's mouths to reach the bridge, commanded the troops to cut the cables, and burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Renqian at first opposed the plan but finally agreed. They took light boats with muffled oars to the bridge, cut the cables, and burned the whole structure.

sentences.zh: 周師大衄，死者不可計，焚其資糧而還。

translations.literal: The Zhou army suffered a great rout, the dead beyond counting; they burned their provisions and stores and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army suffered a crushing defeat with countless dead. They burned the Zhou stores and returned.

sentences.zh: 以功授武殿使。

translations.literal: For this merit he was appointed Martial Hall commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was made Martial Hall commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周師退保定遠，又募壯士為負販狀入定遠，偵軍多寡及守將之名。

translations.literal: The Zhou army withdrew to secure Dingyuan; he again recruited stalwarts disguised as peddlers to enter Dingyuan and spy on the army's numbers and the names of the defending generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army withdrew to Dingyuan, he recruited men disguised as peddlers to enter the town and learn the size of the garrison and the names of its commanders.

sentences.zh: 還曰：「武行德、周務勍也。」

translations.literal: On returning they said, "Wu Xingde and Zhou Wujin."
translations.idiomatic: They returned and reported, "The commanders are Wu Xingde and Zhou Wujin."

sentences.zh: 廷謂曰：「是可圖也。」

translations.literal: Tingwei said, "These can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Tingwei said, "They can be taken."

sentences.zh: 又籍鄉兵萬餘洎卒五千，日夕訓練，依山銜枚設伏以破之，周師大潰，行德單騎脫走。

translations.literal: He again registered more than ten thousand local militia together with five thousand soldiers, trained them day and night, set ambush along the hills with gags in their mouths to defeat them; the Zhou army collapsed in great disorder, and Xingde escaped alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled more than ten thousand local militia and five thousand regulars, drilled them day and night, and set hill ambushes with muffled troops. The Zhou army was routed, and Xingde escaped alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 時有以玉帛子女餉廷謂者，悉拒之，唯取良馬二百匹以獻。

translations.literal: At the time some offered jade, silks, and women to Tingwei as gifts; he refused them all and took only two hundred fine horses to present.
translations.idiomatic: Some offered him jade, silks, and women as gifts, but he refused them all and presented only two hundred fine horses.

sentences.zh: 以功為滁州刺史、上淮巡檢應援兵馬都監。

translations.literal: For his merit he became Prefect of Chuzhou and overall military supervisor of relief forces for the upper Huai inspection circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made prefect of Chuzhou and overall military supervisor of upper Huai relief forces.

sentences.zh: 及紫金山之戰，南唐諸將多歸降者，獨廷謂以全軍還守濠州，追不能及。

translations.literal: At the battle of Purple Gold Mountain, many Southern Tang generals surrendered; only Tingwei brought his whole army back to hold Haozhou, and pursuers could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Purple Gold Mountain most Southern Tang generals surrendered, but Tingwei brought his whole army back to Haozhou and could not be overtaken.

sentences.zh: 時濠守欲棄城走，廷謂止之。

translations.literal: At the time the Haozhou defender wished to abandon the city and flee; Tingwei stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The defender of Haozhou wished to abandon the city and flee, but Tingwei stopped him.

sentences.zh: 俄加本州團練使，繕戈甲，治溝壘，常若敵至。

translations.literal: Shortly he was added regimental training commissioner of his prefecture, repaired weapons and armor, repaired ditches and ramparts, always as if the enemy were arriving.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regimental training commissioner of Haozhou, repaired arms and armor, strengthened ditches and walls, and kept the city on a war footing.

sentences.zh: 是秋，周師復至，表於景請援，且言周兵四臨，乞卑辭請和，以固鄰好。

translations.literal: That autumn the Zhou army came again; he memorialized Jing requesting relief, and added the Zhou troops pressed on four sides, begging humble words to seek peace and secure good relations with the neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Zhou army returned. He memorialized Li Jing for reinforcements, urged that the Zhou pressed on all sides, and asked that humble terms be sought to secure peace with the neighbor.

sentences.zh: 夜出敢死士千餘襲周營，焚頭車洞屋，周師蹂躪死者甚眾。

translations.literal: By night he sent out more than a thousand dare-to-die men to raid the Zhou camp, burned the lead carts and cave dwellings, and the Zhou army trampled one another with many dead.
translations.idiomatic: By night he sent more than a thousand volunteers to raid the Zhou camp, burned their lead wagons and shelters, and many Zhou soldiers were trampled to death in the rout.

sentences.zh: 既而援兵不至，周師急擊，廷謂集諸軍壘門之外，南望大慟而降於周。

translations.literal: Before long relief did not arrive; the Zhou army pressed the attack fiercely; Tingwei gathered the armies outside the camp gates, looked south and wept greatly, and surrendered to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When relief failed to come and the Zhou pressed the attack, Tingwei assembled his troops outside the gates, wept toward the south, and surrendered to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 至山陽，見世宗，特加宴勞，賜金帶、襲衣、良馬、器皿，拜亳州防禦使。

translations.literal: On reaching Shanyang he saw Shizong, who specially added a feast in his honor and granted a gold belt, court robes, fine horses, and vessels, appointing him defensive commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanyang he was received by Emperor Shizong with a special feast and rewarded with a gold belt, court robes, fine horses, and vessels, and was made defensive commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 以其弟本州馬步都校廷讚為和州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tingzan, horse-and-foot colonel of the prefecture, was made Prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tingzan, horse-and-foot colonel of the prefecture, was made prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 命攻天長軍，降其將馬贇。

translations.literal: He was ordered to attack the Tianchang Army and induced its general Ma Yun to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to attack the Tianchang Army and induced its commander Ma Yun to surrender.

sentences.zh: 又為樓櫓戰櫂左右廂都監，俄歸譙郡。

translations.literal: He again served as overall supervisor of the left and right wings of siege towers and war boats, and shortly returned to Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made overall supervisor of siege towers and war boats for both wings, then soon returned to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 宋初，從征上黨，再知亳州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he followed the Shangdang campaign and again governed Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he joined the Shangdang campaign and again governed Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，代還，改絳州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, when relieved and returning, he was changed to defensive commissioner of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande, after being relieved, he was made defensive commissioner of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 兩川平，馮瓚知梓州，為僕夫所訟，召廷謂為靜江軍節度觀察留後以代之。

translations.literal: When the Two Rivers were pacified, Feng Zan governed Zizhou and was sued by a servant; Tingwei was summoned as military governor and surveillance commissioner of the Jingjiang Army as acting prefect to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Two Rivers were pacified, Feng Zan governed Zizhou but was sued by a servant. Tingwei was summoned as acting military governor and surveillance commissioner of the Jingjiang Army to replace him.

sentences.zh: 州承舊政，有莊宅戶、車腳戶，皆隸州將，鷹鷂戶日獻雉兔，田獵戶歲入皮革；

translations.literal: The prefecture inherited old policies: there were manorial households and cart households, all subordinate to prefectural generals; hawk households daily presented pheasants and hares, and hunting households yearly paid in leather;
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture still followed old abuses: manorial households and cart households answered to prefectural officers; hawk households supplied pheasants and hares daily, and hunting households paid leather yearly;

sentences.zh: 又有鄉將、都將、鎮將輩互擾閭里，廷謂悉除之。

translations.literal: there were also village generals, commandery generals, garrison generals, and the like mutually harassing the neighborhoods; Tingwei abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: village, commandery, and garrison officers also harassed the people. Tingwei abolished all of these practices.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao, he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Kaibao at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 廷謂性恭謹，事母以孝聞，未嘗不束帶立侍。

translations.literal: Tingwei's nature was respectful and cautious; he served his mother with filial piety renowned, never failing to stand in attendance with his belt fastened.
translations.idiomatic: Tingwei was respectful and dutiful, famed for filial service to his mother, and never attended her except in full formal dress, standing at her side.

sentences.zh: 子延濬。

translations.literal: His son Yanjun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yanjun.

sentences.zh: 廷謂兄廷諭，仕南唐為太子洗馬致仕，宋初至秘書監。

translations.literal: Tingwei's elder brother Tingyu served Southern Tang as crown prince reader and retired from office; at the beginning of Song he reached Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tingwei's elder brother Tingyu had served Southern Tang as crown prince reader before retiring, and early in Song rose to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 廷諭子延澤。

translations.literal: Tingyu's son Yanze.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu's son was Yanze.

sentences.zh: 子 延濬

translations.literal: Son: Yanjun
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yanjun

sentences.zh: 延濬，字利川。

translations.literal: Yanjun, style name Lichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun, whose style was Lichuan.

sentences.zh: 幼謙和。

translations.literal: From youth he was modest and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was modest and even-tempered.

sentences.zh: 初，廷謂為靜江軍節度使，延濬為桂州牙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: At first, when Tingwei was military governor of the Jingjiang Army, Yanjun was inner yamen commander-in-chief of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingwei was military governor of the Jingjiang Army, Yanjun was inner yamen commander-in-chief at Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 廷謂卒，太祖錄延濬為供奉官，屢使西北，宣諭機事。

translations.literal: When Tingwei died, the Taizu enrolled Yanjun as a tribute attendant and repeatedly sent him to the northwest to announce and instruct on secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingwei died, the emperor enrolled Yanjun as a tribute attendant and repeatedly sent him to the northwest on confidential missions.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，以內庭宣索及殿前賜齎、移文庫務未有專領之者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, because there was as yet no one specifically in charge of inner-court requisitions and bestowals before the throne or transfer documents for storehouse affairs,
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo there was still no officer specifically in charge of inner-court requisitions, gifts before the throne, or storehouse transfer documents.

sentences.zh: 乃置合同憑由印，命延濬與內藏庫副使劉蒙正掌之。

translations.literal: the contract credential seal was established, and Yanjun was ordered with Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Treasury Liu Mengzheng to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: The contract credential seal was therefore established, and Yanjun was ordered with Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Treasury Liu Mengzheng to manage it.

sentences.zh: 又領八作司及督治汴河。

translations.literal: He also headed the Eight Works Office and supervised repair of the Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: He also headed the Eight Works Office and supervised work on the Bian Canal.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，改崇儀使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, he was changed to commissioner of Honored Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was made commissioner of Honored Rites.

sentences.zh: 詔與翟守素、田仁朗、王繼恩往河北，分路按行諸州城壘，發鎮兵葺之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him with Zhai Shousu, Tian Renlang, and Wang Jien to go to Hebei, travel the routes separately to inspect the fortifications of the prefectures, and dispatch garrison troops to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Zhai Shousu, Tian Renlang, and Wang Jien to go to Hebei, inspect prefectural fortifications by separate routes, and send garrison troops to repair them.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，詔建河北方田，命延濬等五人共往規畫，會罷其務而止。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, an edict ordered the establishment of square fields in Hebei and commanded Yanjun and five others together to go plan them; it happened that the task was abolished and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong (989) he was one of five men sent to plan square fields in Hebei, but the project was abandoned before it began.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，李順亂，改西京作坊使，充成都十州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, when Li Shun rebelled, he was changed to commissioner of the Western Capital workshop and filled the post of metropolitan inspection commissioner of the ten prefectures of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua (993), when Li Shun rebelled, he was made commissioner of the Western Capital workshop and metropolitan inspection commissioner of the ten Chengdu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時成都將陷，延濬單騎入城，與郭載議募亡卒退保劍門，賊數千來躡其後，擊破之。

translations.literal: At the time Chengdu was about to fall; Yanjun entered the city alone on horseback, discussed with Guo Zai recruiting scattered soldiers to withdraw and hold Jianmen, several thousand rebels came treading on their heels, and he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu was about to fall, Yanjun rode in alone, met with Guo Zai to recruit scattered troops and withdraw to Jianmen, and when several thousand rebels pursued them he defeated the pursuers.

sentences.zh: 王繼恩率兵至，以延濬為先鋒壕砦使，即領兵倍道先進。

translations.literal: Wang Jien led troops to arrive, made Yanjun vanguard trench-and-stockade commissioner, and he immediately led the army by double marches to advance first.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jien arrived with his army, Yanjun was made vanguard trench commissioner and led the troops forward at forced march.

sentences.zh: 賊出探騎數十，延濬悉禽之，盡得賊機事。

translations.literal: The rebels sent out several tens of scout horsemen; Yanjun captured them all and fully obtained the rebels' secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent out several dozen scouts; Yanjun captured them all and learned the enemy's plans in full.

sentences.zh: 延濬易旗變號，賊不知覺，斬關掩入，斬千餘級。

translations.literal: Yanjun changed flags and altered signals; the rebels did not perceive it; he cut through the pass and burst in by surprise, taking more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun changed flags and signals so the rebels did not notice, then stormed the pass by surprise and killed more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 繼恩又請延濬知漢州，州經兵燹，廨舍、橋梁、城砦悉毀。

translations.literal: Jien again requested that Yanjun govern Hanzhou; the prefecture had suffered military fires, and government offices, bridges, and city stockades were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Jien then asked that Yanjun govern Hanzhou, where war had destroyed government offices, bridges, and fortifications.

sentences.zh: 延濬募軍民葺之，又率州帑以應軍須。

translations.literal: Yanjun recruited soldiers and civilians to repair them and also led the prefectural treasury to meet army needs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun recruited soldiers and civilians to rebuild them and drew on the prefectural treasury to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 錄功，改洛苑使。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was changed to commissioner of the Luo Park.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded and he was made commissioner of the Luo Park.

sentences.zh: 又命率兵屯遂州，劍門鈐轄、轉運使劉錫言其勞，詔書嘉獎。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to lead troops to garrison Suizhou; Liu Xi, military superintendent of Jianmen and transport commissioner, spoke of his labors, and an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to garrison Suizhou with his troops. Liu Xi, military superintendent of Jianmen and transport commissioner, reported his exertions, and the court rewarded him with an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，改內園使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong, he was changed to commissioner of the Inner Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Zhenzong he was made commissioner of the Inner Garden.

sentences.zh: 代還，會河朔用兵，延濬馳往邊城，按視砦壘。

translations.literal: When relieved and returning, it happened that troops were used in Heshuo; Yanjun galloped to the border cities to inspect stockades and forts.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned after being relieved, war broke out in Heshuo, and Yanjun hurried to the frontier to inspect fortifications.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，疾卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the second year of Xianping.

sentences.zh: 子有倫，為供奉官、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His son Youlun served as tribute attendant and palace gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youlun served as tribute attendant and palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 從子 延澤

translations.literal: Nephew: Yanze
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Yanze

sentences.zh: 延澤，字德潤，南唐試秘書省正字。

translations.literal: Yanze, style name Derun, passed the Secretariat probationary orthographer examination of Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanze, whose style was Derun, had passed the Southern Tang examination for probationary orthographer in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，四遷著作佐郎，轉殿中丞、知建州。

translations.literal: During Qiande, he was promoted four times to assistant editorial director, then transferred to palace director and administrator of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande he rose through four promotions to assistant editorial director, then became palace director and administrator of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，太宗聞延澤洎右讚善大夫董元亨皆好學，博通典籍，詔宰相召問經史大義，皆條對稱旨，命為史館檢討。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, Taizong heard that Yanze together with Right Palatine Counselor Dong Yuanheng both loved learning and were broadly versed in the classics; an edict ordered the chief ministers to summon and question them on the great principles of the classics and histories; both answered item by item to satisfaction and were appointed revisers of the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, Emperor Taizong learned that Yanze and Right Palatine Counselor Dong Yuanheng were both devoted to learning and widely read in the classics. He had the chief ministers question them on the classics and histories; both answered point by point to his satisfaction and were appointed revisers at the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 歷國子《周易》博士、國子博士。

translations.literal: He successively served as Erudite of the Zhouyi in the Directorate of Education and as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Erudite of the Zhouyi and as Erudite at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 咸平中求休退，授虞部員外郎致仕。

translations.literal: During Xianping he sought retirement and was granted Vice Director of the Ministry of Works with leave from office.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping he asked to retire and was granted Vice Director of the Ministry of Works with permission to leave office.

sentences.zh: 居濠州城南，有小園以自娛，其詠牡丹千餘首。

translations.literal: He dwelt south of Haozhou city, had a small garden for his own pleasure, and composed more than a thousand poems on peonies.
translations.idiomatic: He lived south of Haozhou with a small garden for his amusement and wrote more than a thousand poems on peonies.

sentences.zh: 聚圖籍萬餘卷，手自刊校。

translations.literal: He gathered more than ten thousand scrolls of maps and books and personally collated them.
translations.idiomatic: He collected more than ten thousand scrolls of books and maps and collated them with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 范杲、韓丕皆與之遊。

translations.literal: Fan Gao and Han Pi both associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Gao and Han Pi were among his companions.

sentences.zh: 景德初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Jingde era.

sentences.zh: 元亨亦至虞部員外郎，嘗纘《玄門碑志》三十卷。

translations.literal: Yuanheng also reached Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and once compiled Records of Mysterious Gate Inscriptions in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng also rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and once compiled Records of Mysterious Gate Inscriptions in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 趙延進

translations.literal: Zhao Yanjin
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanjin

sentences.zh: 趙延進，澶州頓丘人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanjin, a native of Dunqiu in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanjin was a native of Dunqiu in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 父暉，周太子太師。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent under the Zhou dynasty.

sentences.zh: 暉為偏將時，趙在禮據鄴。

translations.literal: When Hui was a subordinate general, Zhao Zaili held Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was still a subordinate general, Zhao Zaili held Ye.

sentences.zh: 延進頗親學，嘗與軍中少年入民家，競取財賄，延進獨持書數十編以歸，同輩哂之。

translations.literal: Yanjin was quite devoted to learning; he once entered civilian households with youths of the army, all competing to seize property and bribes; Yanjin alone carried several tens of bundles of books back, and his companions laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin was devoted to learning. Once he entered a civilian house with young soldiers who were all grabbing loot; he alone carried off several dozen bundles of books, and his companions laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 漢末，暉領鳳翔節度，未赴鎮，王景崇據城反，命暉為都招討使擊之。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Hui received the Fengxiang military governorship but had not yet gone to his post when Wang Jingchong seized the city and rebelled; Hui was ordered as overall pacification commissioner to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Later Han, Hui was appointed military governor of Fengxiang but had not yet taken up his post when Wang Jingchong rebelled and held the city. Hui was ordered to attack him as overall pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 延進年十八，屢當軍鋒。

translations.literal: Yanjin was eighteen and repeatedly met the army's front.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin was eighteen and repeatedly faced the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 景崇平，延進奉捷奏以入，授鳳翔牙內指揮使，領貴州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jingchong was pacified, Yanjin presented the victory memorial and entered; he was appointed inner yamen commander of Fengxiang and held the prefecture of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingchong was subdued, Yanjin presented the victory report to court and was appointed inner yamen commander at Fengxiang and prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 暉徙宋州，亦從為牙職，改領榮州刺史。

translations.literal: When Hui was transferred to Songzhou, he also followed as a yamen officer and was changed to hold the prefecture of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was transferred to Songzhou, Yanjin followed him on his staff and was made prefect of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 睢陽有盜數百，各立酋帥，為民患。

translations.literal: At Suiyang there were several hundred bandits, each establishing a chieftain, a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred bandits at Suiyang had each set up a chieftain and plagued the people.

sentences.zh: 延進以父命，領牙兵千餘悉禽戮之，詔書褒美。

translations.literal: By his father's order, Yanjin led more than a thousand yamen troops and captured and executed them all; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: At his father's order Yanjin led more than a thousand staff troops, captured the bandits, and executed them all. The court praised him in an edict.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，表求持服。

translations.literal: When his father died he memorialized requesting to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he petitioned to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 既終喪，周世宗征淮南，延進獻萬縑以助軍，仍請對，世宗召見之。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Shizong of Zhou campaigned against Huainan; Yanjin presented ten thousand bolts of silk to aid the army and still requested an audience; Shizong summoned and received him.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, when Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, Yanjin presented ten thousand bolts of silk to aid the army and asked for an audience. The emperor received him.

sentences.zh: 時延進有從兄為虎捷都虞候、帳前橫衝指揮使，世宗指延進語之曰：「爾弟拳勇有謀，將授以禁軍大校。」

translations.literal: At the time Yanjin had a cousin who was deputy commander of the Tiger Swift and commander of the Vanguard Charge before the tent; Shizong pointed at Yanjin and said to him, "Your younger brother is bold in fist and brave in counsel; I shall grant him a high colonelcy in the Imperial Guard."
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin's cousin was deputy commander of the Tiger Swift and commander of the Vanguard Charge before the tent. The emperor pointed to Yanjin and told him, "Your cousin is brave and resourceful. I mean to make him a senior colonel in the Imperial Guard."

sentences.zh: 延進自陳好讀書，不願也。

translations.literal: Yanjin himself stated that he loved reading books and did not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin declared that he preferred reading and did not wish for such a post.

sentences.zh: 翌日，授右千牛衛將軍、濠州兵馬鈐轄，從征瓦橋關，為隨駕金吾街仗使。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and military superintendent of Haozhou; he followed the Wagong Pass campaign as Golden Crow street guard attendant accompanying the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was made general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and military superintendent of Haozhou, joined the Wagong Pass campaign, and served as Golden Crow street guard attendant on the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷右羽林軍將軍、濠州都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was transferred to general of the Right Feathered Forest Army and overall supervisor of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was made general of the Right Feathered Forest Army and overall supervisor of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 會伐蜀，以襄州當川路津要，命為鈐轄、同知州務。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Shu, because Xiangzhou lay on the vital passage of the Sichuan route, he was ordered as military superintendent and concurrent administrator of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shu campaign, because Xiangzhou guarded the vital Sichuan route, he was made military superintendent and concurrent administrator of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，專領郡事。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he alone directed commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he governed the prefecture alone.

sentences.zh: 漢江水歲壞堤，害民田，常興工修護，延進累石為岸，遂絕其患。

translations.literal: Each year the Han River waters destroyed the dikes and harmed the people's fields; works were regularly raised for repair and protection; Yanjin piled stone to make banks and thereby ended the scourge.
translations.idiomatic: The Han River broke its dikes yearly and ruined farmland. Yanjin built stone embankments and ended the damage for good.

sentences.zh: 入為兩浙、漳泉國信使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as credentialed envoy to the Two Zhe and Zhang-Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as credentialed envoy to the Two Zhe and Zhang-Quan circuits.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，授右龍武將軍、知靈州，以母老願留，得權判右金吾街仗使，歷知河中府、梓、相、青三州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, he was appointed general of the Right Dragon Martial Guard and administrator of Lingzhou; because his mother was old he wished to remain, obtained acting adjudication as Right Golden Crow street guard attendant, and successively governed Hezhong prefecture and the three prefectures Zi, Xiang, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he was appointed general of the Right Dragon Martial Guard and administrator of Lingzhou, but because his mother was old he asked to stay nearer court and was given acting charge of the Right Golden Crow street guard. He later governed Hezhong and the prefectures of Zi, Xiang, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，大軍平并州，討幽薊，皆為攻城八作壕砦使。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo, when the great army pacified Bingzhou and campaigned against You and Ji, on each occasion he was siege Eight Works trench-and-stockade commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he served as siege-works and trench commissioner in the campaigns that pacified Bingzhou and attacked You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔督造炮具八百，期以半月，延進八日成。

translations.literal: He was once ordered to supervise manufacture of eight hundred artillery pieces, the term set at half a month; Yanjin completed them in eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was ordered to supervise eight hundred artillery pieces with a deadline of half a month; Yanjin finished them in eight days.

sentences.zh: 太宗親試之，大悅。

translations.literal: Taizong personally tested them and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong tested them himself and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 又令主城北諸洞子。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to take charge of the various saps north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He was also put in charge of the mining tunnels north of the city.

sentences.zh: 及班師，命與孟玄哲、藥可瓊留屯定州。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was ordered with Meng Xuanzhe and Yao Keqiong to remain garrisoned at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, he was ordered with Meng Xuanzhe and Yao Keqiong to remain at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遼人擾邊，命延進與崔翰、李繼隆將兵八萬禦之，賜陣圖，分為八陣，俾以從事。

translations.literal: When Liao people harassed the border, Yanjin was ordered with Cui Han and Li Jilong to command eighty thousand troops to defend against them; battle array diagrams were granted, divided into eight formations, and they were made to follow them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the frontier, Yanjin was ordered with Cui Han and Li Jilong to command eighty thousand men against them. They were given battle diagrams arranged in eight formations and told to follow them.

sentences.zh: 師次滿城，遼騎坌至，延進乘高望之，東西亙野，不見其際。

translations.literal: The army halted at Mancheng; Liao horsemen surged up; Yanjin took a height to look at them; east and west they stretched across the plain, their limit unseen.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Mancheng as Khitan horsemen poured in. Yanjin climbed a height to look out and saw them spread across the plain from east to west without end.

sentences.zh: 翰等方按圖布陣，陣去各百步，士眾疑懼，略無鬥志。

translations.literal: Han and the others were just then arranging formations according to the diagrams, each formation a hundred paces from the next; soldiers and masses were doubtful and fearful, with scarcely any fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Han and the others were deploying the formations from the diagrams, each a hundred paces apart. The troops were uneasy and had little heart to fight.

sentences.zh: 延進謂翰等曰：「主上委吾等以邊事，蓋期於克敵爾。

translations.literal: Yanjin said to Han and the others, "The ruler has entrusted us with border affairs, surely expecting that we defeat the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin told Han and the others, "The emperor has entrusted us with the frontier because he expects us to defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今敵眾若此，而我師星布，其勢懸絕，彼若持我，將何以濟？

translations.literal: Now the enemy is numerous like this, while our army is scattered like stars—the situation is desperately unequal; if they pin us, how shall we succeed?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is so numerous and our forces are scattered like stars. The odds are desperate. If they pin us down, how shall we succeed?

sentences.zh: 不如合而擊之，可以決勝。

translations.literal: Better to unite and strike them—we can settle victory.
translations.idiomatic: We had better combine and strike them. That is how we can win.

sentences.zh: 違令而獲利，不猶愈於辱國乎？」

translations.literal: Disobeying orders yet gaining profit—is it not still better than shaming the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Disobeying orders yet winning profit—is that not better than shaming the state?"

sentences.zh: 翰等曰：「萬一不捷，則若之何？」

translations.literal: Han and the others said, "If by chance we do not succeed, then what?"
translations.idiomatic: Han and the others said, "But if we fail, what then?"

sentences.zh: 延進曰：「倘有喪敗，則延進獨當其責。」

translations.literal: Yanjin said, "If there should be defeat, then Yanjin alone shall bear the blame."
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin said, "If we are defeated, I alone will bear the blame."

sentences.zh: 於是改為二陣，前後相副。

translations.literal: Thereupon they changed to two formations, front and rear supporting each other.
translations.idiomatic: They then formed two arrays, front and rear supporting each other.

sentences.zh: 士眾皆喜，三戰，大破之，獲人馬、牛羊、鎧甲數十萬。

translations.literal: Soldiers and masses were all pleased; in three battles they inflicted a great defeat, capturing several hundred thousand in men, horses, cattle, sheep, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: The troops took heart. In three engagements they won a crushing victory and seized hundreds of thousands of men, horses, cattle, sheep, and suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 以功遷右監門衛大將軍、知鎮州。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to grand general of the Right Gate Guard and administrator of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made grand general of the Right Gate Guard and administrator of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 及代，吏民數千守闕借留，詔許留一年。

translations.literal: When he was to be relieved, several thousand officials and people guarded the gate requesting to detain him; an edict permitted him to remain one year.
translations.idiomatic: When he was to be relieved, several thousand officials and commoners blocked the gate to ask that he stay. The court allowed him to remain one more year.

sentences.zh: 俄改右領軍衛大將軍，出為高陽關、平戎軍都監兼緣邊巡檢，改鈐轄。

translations.literal: Shortly he was changed to grand general of the Right Leading Army Guard, went out as overall supervisor of Gaoyang Pass and Pingrong Army with concurrent frontier inspection, and was changed to military superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand general of the Right Leading Army Guard and sent out as overall supervisor of Gaoyang Pass and Pingrong Army with concurrent frontier inspection, then as military superintendent.

sentences.zh: 知揚州，召入，授右屯衛大將軍，徙知相州。

translations.literal: He governed Yangzhou, was summoned in, was appointed grand general of the Right Garrison Guard, and was moved to govern Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yangzhou, was recalled, made grand general of the Right Garrison Guard, and transferred to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷右驍衛大將軍，改知鄧州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand general of the Right Valiant Guard and changed to govern Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general of the Right Valiant Guard and made administrator of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，飛蝗不入境，詔褒之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, flying locusts did not enter his territory; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunhua, locust swarms did not enter his territory, and the court praised him in an edict.

sentences.zh: 還，判右金吾街仗事。

translations.literal: On returning, he adjudicated Right Golden Crow street guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he oversaw Right Golden Crow street guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，拜右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, he was appointed grand general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was appointed grand general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年卒，年七十三，贈左武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he died, aged seventy-three, and was posthumously granted upper general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Xianping at the age of seventy-three and was posthumously granted upper general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 延進姿狀秀整，涉獵經史，好作詩什，士流以此多之。

translations.literal: Yanjin's bearing and appearance were elegant and trim; he ranged through the classics and histories, loved composing verse, and men of culture for this held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin was handsome and well favored, widely read in the classics and histories, fond of poetry, and esteemed by literati for it.

sentences.zh: 延進妻即淑德皇后之妹，故在顯德、興國中，頗任以腹心。

translations.literal: Yanjin's wife was the younger sister of the Shude Empress; therefore during Xiande and Xingguo he was greatly entrusted as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin's wife was the younger sister of Empress Shude, and during Xiande and the early Song years he was much trusted as an intimate counselor.

sentences.zh: 子昂，太平興國二年登進士第，至戶部郎中、直昭文館。

translations.literal: His son Ang passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Taiping Xingguo and rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue and direct attendant of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Taiping Xingguo and rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue and direct attendant of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 輔超，忻州秀容人，家世業農。

translations.literal: Fu Chao, a native of Xiurong in Xinzhou, his family for generations practiced agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chao was a native of Xiurong in Xinzhou from a farming family.

sentences.zh: 超少勇悍有力，晉開運中應募，隸澶州軍籍。

translations.literal: Chao from youth was brave, fierce, and strong; during Kaiyun of Jin he answered the recruitment and was entered on the army rolls of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chao was brave and powerfully built. During Kaiyun of Later Jin he enlisted and was entered on the rolls of the Cizhou army.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，趙思綰據永興叛，周祖護諸將討之，督兵攻城。

translations.literal: During Qianyou of Han, Zhao Sixuan held Yongxing and rebelled; the Zhou founder escorted the generals to campaign against him and directed troops in storming the city.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou of Later Han, Zhao Sixuan rebelled and held Yongxing. The Zhou founder led generals against him and directed the siege.

sentences.zh: 超率驍勇十七人升雲梯，斫北門樓，樓壞而入，士卒繼進，城遂陷，以功補小校。

translations.literal: Chao led seventeen fierce warriors up a cloud ladder, cut down the north gate tower, the tower broke and they entered, soldiers followed in succession, the city was thereupon taken, and for his merit he was appointed a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: Chao led seventeen picked men up a siege ladder, smashed the north gate tower, broke into the city, and was followed by the troops. The city fell, and he was made a junior officer for his merit.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，從太祖征淮南，常執銳前驅，定滁、泗，破淮陰，下揚州，以功轉日騎副兵馬使。

translations.literal: During Xiande, he followed the Taizu in the Huainan campaign, often grasping sharp weapons in the vanguard, secured Chu and Si, broke Huaiyin, took Yangzhou, and for his merit was transferred to deputy horse-and-arms commissioner of the Daily Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiande he followed the future Emperor Taizu on the Huainan campaign, often leading the van with drawn weapons. He helped secure Chu and Si, storm Huaiyin, and take Yangzhou, and was made deputy horse-and-arms commissioner of the Daily Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 論曰：太祖有天下，凡五代之臣，無不以恩信結之，既以安其反側，亦借其威力，以鎮撫四方。

translations.literal: The discussion says: When the Taizu gained the realm, all ministers of the Five Dynasties were bound to him without exception by grace and trust—both to settle their wavering and to borrow their might to pacify the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When the Taizu won the realm, he bound every minister of the Five Dynasties with grace and trust—both to steady those who might waver and to use their power to pacify the empire.

sentences.zh: 故一時諸將吳虔裕、蔡審廷之徒，數從征討，咸有勞績焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the generals of the time, such as Wu Qianyu and Cai Shenting, repeatedly followed campaigns and punitive expeditions, and all had labors and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Thus generals of the day such as Wu Qianyu and Cai Shenting followed repeated campaigns and all won merit.

sentences.zh: 若馬令琮守河內，儲兵食以迎王師；

translations.literal: As Ma Lingcong held Henei and stored army provisions to welcome the imperial army;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lingcong held Henei and stockpiled provisions for the imperial army;

sentences.zh: 解暉擊湖南，冒鋒鏑以禽敵將：此忠藎驍果，尤可稱者。

translations.literal: as Jie Hui struck Hunan and braved blades and arrows to capture an enemy general: these were loyal, earnest, fierce, and resolute—especially worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: and Jie Hui in Hunan braved sword and arrow to capture an enemy general—these were acts of loyal, fierce valor especially worth praise.

sentences.zh: 漢徽之疾危辭藥，藏英之為親復仇，亦皆一節之美。

translations.literal: Hanhu's grave illness yet refusing medicine, and Cangying's avenging his kin—each was also a beautiful point in its own right.
translations.idiomatic: Hanhu's refusal of medicine when gravely ill and Cangying's vengeance for his kin were each admirable in their own way.

sentences.zh: 惟張勳嗜殺，晉卿冒貨，雖立威著勤，所不取也。

translations.literal: Only Zhang Xun's love of killing and Jinqing's grasping for goods—though they established awe and showed diligence—were what is not to be taken as example.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Xun's bloodlust and Jinqing's corruption, though they won repute for sternness and diligence, are examples to be rejected.
